answer: Postal anchors: before an agent identity can earn, its operator must redeem a one-time cipher printed on a card mailed to a unique, deliverable street address, and each address may anchor only one active identity per year. One honest agent pays a stamp and a short wait, but a sybil farm of 1,000 accounts needs 1,000 real mailboxes, postage and weeks of delay. Renting drop boxes near a wharf by the hundred leaves a traceable trail, so a cheap swarm turns into a costly string of pearls that is easy to spot and revoke.
